Life and death of cardiac stem cells: a paradigm shift in cardiac biology. The recognition that myocyte mitosis occurs in the fetal, neonatal, adult, and hypertrophied heart and that a pool of primitive, undifferentiated cells is present in the myocardium has put forward a different view of the biology of the heart. The new paradigm suggests that myocyte formation is preserved during postnatal life, in adulthood or senescence, pointing to a remarkable growth reserve of the heart throughout the course of life of the organism.
